parts.text: Write a short thread about learning in public and post it to X straight away.

Here is a short thread about learning in public:

1/5: learning in public isn't about bragging; it’s about leaving a trail of breadcrumbs for yourself and others. it turns your learning journey into a magnet for opportunities. here is why you should start sharing what you know today. 🧵

2/5: sharing what you learn forces you to understand it better. when you explain a concept to someone else, you uncover the gaps in your own knowledge. it’s the feynman technique in real-time, helping you move from "i think i get it" to "i can build this."

3/5: you build a network while you sleep. every post or project you share acts as a signal to people who care about the same things. instead of cold emails, people find your work and reach out because you've already proven you're doing the work.

4/5: the feedback loop is your fastest path to growth. when you post a snippet of code or a design draft, experts can correct your mistakes early. you get access to thousands of years of combined experience just by being vulnerable enough to be wrong in public.

5/5: you don't need to be an expert to start. you just need to be one step ahead of the person behind you. start by sharing one thing you learned today.

thread.text: learning in public isn't about bragging; it’s about leaving a trail of breadcrumbs for yourself and others. it turns your learning journey into a magnet for opportunities. here is why you should start sharing what you know today. 🧵

sharing what you learn forces you to understand it better. when you explain a concept to someone else, you uncover the gaps in your own knowledge. it’s the feynman technique in real-time, helping you move from "i think i get it" to "i can build this."

you build a network while you sleep. every post or project you share acts as a signal to people who care about the same things. instead of cold emails, people find your work and reach out because you've already proven you're doing the work.

the feedback loop is your fastest path to growth. when you post a snippet of code or a design draft, experts can correct your mistakes early. you get access to thousands of years of combined experience just by being vulnerable enough to be wrong in public.

you don't need to be an expert to start. you just need to be one step ahead of the person behind you. start by sharing one thing you learned today.

what was the last thing you learned that surprised you? #learninginpublic
